name: Generalized Riemann Hypothesis
question: Does the critical-line assertion hold for every Dirichlet L-function?
first_attack: Audit precise statement and prove a restricted case
dispatch_next: Reproduce a published primitive character modulo 3 or 5 with the correct root number, branch conventions and independently checked zero count; document why this is known mathematics, not GRH progress.
dispatch_why: The new engine verifies χ4 only; the generalized Riemann hypothesis concerns all Dirichlet characters. Replaying a separate primitive-character certificate tests the reusable contour and gamma-factor implementation.

campaign.method: The zeta interval engine applied to L(s, chi_4)
campaign.hypothesis: Every non-trivial zero of every Dirichlet L-function has real part 1/2.
campaign.first_proof_obligation: Certify one further primitive character, of conductor 3 or 5, to a height where the root number and the gamma factor are checked by the same argument principle.
campaign.next_experiment: Reuse the zero-count certificate for the non-principal character modulo 3, including an independent replay of its Gauss sum.
campaign.falsification: A primitive character and a height T at which the certified argument count exceeds the number of critical-line sign changes.
campaign.blocker: One character at height 17 does not constrain the other characters. Conductor 3 is the smallest untouched case.

probes.name: Generalized Riemann Hypothesis
probes.title: Critical-line zero count for L(s, chi_4) up to a small height
probes.frontier: Known: the first zeros of Dirichlet L-functions, including L(s, χ₄), have been tabulated far beyond this height. The certificate is for the single character χ₄. Reproduction only, and not a proof of GRH.

smoke.scope: Every non-trivial zero of L(s, χ₄) with imaginary part in (0, 11] is simple and lies on the critical line: the argument principle gives N(11) = 2, equal to the number of disjoint intervals where the associated real Z-function changes sign.

deep.scope: Every non-trivial zero of L(s, χ₄) with imaginary part in (0, 17] is simple and lies on the critical line: the argument principle gives N(17) = 4, equal to the number of disjoint intervals where the associated real Z-function changes sign.

milestones.title: The first two non-trivial zeros of L(s, chi_4) are simple and on the critical line
milestones.scope: One Dirichlet character, N(11) = 2; not the generalized Riemann hypothesis
milestones.description: Argument count for L(s, chi_4) matched to sign changes of the real form on (6, 7) and (10, 11), replayed at a second truncation. The deep run reaches N(17) = 4.
